entries.name: ON1
entries.definition: Photo editing and organising software made by ON1, Inc., including ON1 Photo RAW.

entries.name: Onboarding
entries.definition: Guiding new employees or new customers through their first stage of joining so they can work or use a product effectively.

entries.name: Oncogenomics
entries.definition: The study of the genetic and genomic changes behind cancer and how they can guide diagnosis and treatment.

entries.name: Oncology sales
entries.definition: Selling cancer drugs, devices or diagnostics to oncologists, hospitals and other cancer care providers.

entries.name: OneTrust
entries.definition: A software platform for privacy, data governance, third-party risk and compliance management.

entries.name: Online demonstration
entries.definition: Showing a product, process or technique to an audience remotely, using screen sharing or video.

entries.name: Onshape
entries.definition: A cloud-based computer-aided design system for 3D product modelling that runs in a web browser and is owned by PTC.

entries.name: Open banking
entries.definition: A system in which banks let authorised third parties access customer account data and payment services through secure APIs, with the customer's consent.

entries.name: Open Network Computing
entries.definition: A set of distributed computing technologies from Sun Microsystems, including ONC RPC and the Network File System.

entries.name: Open Shortest Path First
entries.definition: A link-state routing protocol for IP networks that finds shortest paths using Dijkstra's algorithm.

entries.name: OpenAPI Specification
entries.definition: A language-agnostic specification for describing HTTP APIs in a machine-readable YAML or JSON format, formerly known as Swagger.

entries.name: OpenCart
entries.definition: An open-source PHP e-commerce platform for running online stores.

entries.name: OpenDaylight
entries.definition: An open-source software-defined networking platform, hosted by the Linux Foundation, built around a network controller.

entries.name: OpenNI
entries.definition: An open-source software framework for working with depth-sensing cameras and natural-interaction devices, such as the Microsoft Kinect.

entries.name: OpenStreetMap
entries.definition: A collaborative project that builds a free, editable map database of the world.

entries.name: OpenTok
entries.definition: A WebRTC-based platform and API, originally from TokBox and now part of Vonage, for adding live video to web and mobile apps.

entries.name: OpenTSDB
entries.definition: A scalable, open-source time series database built to run on Apache HBase.

entries.name: Operating systems
entries.definition: Understanding process, memory, storage and system resource management.

entries.name: Operational risk mitigation
entries.definition: Planning and applying controls to reduce the risk of loss from failed processes, people, systems or external events.

entries.name: Operationalizing AI
entries.definition: Moving AI models from prototypes into reliable production use, including deployment, monitoring and integration into business processes.

entries.name: Operations, administration, maintenance and provisioning
entries.definition: The set of functions needed to run a telecommunications network: operating it, administering it, maintaining it and provisioning services on it.

entries.name: Operations analytics
entries.definition: Using data analysis to measure and improve how an organisation's operations, such as supply chains, production or service delivery, perform.

entries.name: Ophthalmic surgical assisting
entries.definition: Assisting an ophthalmic surgeon during eye surgery by preparing the patient, handling instruments and supporting the procedure.

entries.name: Optical fiber
entries.definition: Thin strands of glass or plastic that carry data as pulses of light.

entries.name: Optical fiber cable
entries.definition: A cable that holds one or more optical fibers inside protective layers for carrying data as light.

entries.name: Optical power meter
entries.definition: An instrument that measures the power of an optical signal, used to test fibre-optic links.

entries.name: Optical waveguides
entries.definition: Structures that guide light along a path, such as optical fibres and channels on a photonic chip.

entries.name: Optimization software
entries.definition: Software that finds the best values of decision variables under given constraints, for example by linear or integer programming.

entries.name: Optitex
entries.definition: Computer-aided design software for 2D pattern making and 3D garment simulation in fashion and apparel.

entries.name: Oracle Advanced Queuing
entries.definition: A message-queuing feature built into Oracle Database for passing messages between applications.

entries.name: Oracle Application Framework
entries.definition: Oracle's Java-based framework for building and customising the web user interfaces of Oracle E-Business Suite applications.

entries.name: Oracle Application Integration Architecture
entries.definition: Oracle's service-oriented framework, with pre-built integration packs, for connecting Oracle and other enterprise business applications.

entries.name: Oracle Autonomous Database
entries.definition: Oracle's cloud database service that uses machine learning to automate tasks such as tuning, patching, scaling, backup and security.

entries.name: Oracle BI Answers
entries.definition: The ad hoc query and analysis component of Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition, used to build reports from a business model.

entries.name: Oracle Business Activity Monitoring
entries.definition: An Oracle Fusion Middleware component that shows real-time dashboards and alerts about business processes and events as they happen.

entries.name: Oracle Clinical
entries.definition: Oracle software for clinical data management, used to collect and clean the data from clinical trials.

entries.name: Oracle Cloud
entries.definition: Oracle's cloud computing offering, covering infrastructure and platform services (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure) and cloud business applications.

entries.name: Oracle EU Sovereign Cloud
entries.definition: An Oracle cloud offering that runs Oracle Cloud Infrastructure services inside the European Union, operated by staff located there, so that customer data stays under EU control.

entries.name: Oracle Fixed Assets
entries.definition: The Oracle E-Business Suite and Fusion Applications module for recording, depreciating, transferring and retiring a company's fixed assets.

entries.name: Oracle GoldenGate
entries.definition: Oracle software that copies and synchronises data between databases in real time, used for replication, migration and integration.
